name: sec-preauth-s4-takeover-busy
title: Editor host pre-auth slots, PR S-4: preemption by higher role, same-user takeover, ErrorCoded `busy` (protocol 1.13.0), loopback backoff as a concurrency/rate cap (audit F1/F2/F6)
issue: Design (APPROVED by the user 2026-10-15; all the design decisions in the doc's 2.7 were approved): C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/security-design-lua-editmode-and-preauth-slots.md PART 2 (read 2.4 'Arbiter', 'What Busy and Preempt do', 'No-token host', 'Rate limiter (item 8 folded in)', 2.6 'PR S-4', 2.7 decisions, 2.8 risks) and the audit C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/editor-host-security-audit-2026-10-15.md (F1/F2/F6). MERGED prerequisites: S-1 #168 (Connection), S-2 #171 (PreAuthSlots, TokenBucket, SessionArbiter, thread-safe RateLimiter, token-before-backoff), S-3 #176 (acceptor + N workers + session thread, Hello replay, busy grace 1 s, plain-Error Busy, coalesced logs, --preauth-slots): READ the merged code and docs first (editor-server/src/EditorServer.cpp OfferToSession and the session hand-off, the busy grace, the arbiter use). SCOPE = section 2.6 'PR S-4': (1) PREEMPTION (P3): a candidate whose verified role is STRICTLY HIGHER than the active session's (admin > editor > viewer) preempts it: the arbiter's Preempt decision sets the session's `close` flag; the session thread leaves at its next wait (<= 100 ms or when the in-flight main-thread command finishes) and runs the normal cleanup (open edit groups closed, autosave flushed); the candidate waits in its slot up to 3 s for 'free'; if the old session does not end in time the candidate gets Busy. (2) SAME-USER TAKEOVER (P4): same user and role => Takeover: close the old session the same way and hand off (so a client that lost its connection can reconnect immediately instead of waiting for the idle timeout). (3) NO-TOKEN HOST: every client is admin with an empty user; design decision 8 says the NEWEST connection takes over (P4) instead of one-at-a-time: implement it (document the behaviour change: today the second connection waits in the backlog) and have the waiting loop in OfferToSession notice a hung-up waiter so it gives its slot back (the S-3 review noted this). (4) `busy` ErrorCoded: a new entry in the protocol's `errorCodes` (editor-server/protocol/protocol.json: follow how the existing coded errors such as those added in 1.12.0 `user/role/ErrorCoded` were added: regenerate the C++/TS/other generated clients and the golden vectors with the repo's generator, bump the protocol to **1.13.0 (a MINOR bump, additive)**, update every place the protocol version is asserted (tests/protocol, docs, the frontend sync note), keep old clients working: Busy sends ErrorCoded `busy` ONLY if the Hello asked for errorCodes, else the plain Error text as today). This item is allowed to touch protocol.json and the generated files (allowProtocol true): note that a Lua-editor-extensions design earlier reserved commands 0x80-0x84 for a LATER minor bump: whichever merges first takes the next minor: this is first: use 1.13.0 and note it in the PR. (5) LOOPBACK BACKOFF as a CAP (item 8 second half): today the global loopback backoff (behind a proxy everyone is loopback) can refuse everyone; change it to a cap on PRE-AUTH CONCURRENCY and handshake RATE for loopback (use the TokenBucket/PreAuthSlots; failures from loopback no longer lock out a client presenting a CORRECT token): follow 2.4 'Rate limiter' exactly; keep per-address backoff for non-loopback addresses. (6) Busy message: decision 5 in 2.7 says whether to name the holder's user or role: follow the APPROVED choice in the doc (read it); if the doc leaves it open choose NOT to name the holder and record a deviation. (7) TCP keepalive on the session socket (SO_KEEPALIVE + per-OS idle options) as in 2.4 'Interaction with item 2': implement with the per-OS differences handled and documented. TESTS: arbiter-driven end-to-end socket tests (the full role matrix over real sockets with the injected clock where possible: viewer->editor preempts, admin->editor preempts, editor->viewer gets Busy, same user takes over, different user same role gets Busy, no-token newest takes over), cleanup happens on preemption (edit groups closed, autosave flushed: assert via the existing observable seams), the candidate gets Busy if the old session does not end in 3 s (use a stuck-session test hook), busy ErrorCoded for a client that asked for errorCodes and a plain Error otherwise, protocol golden vectors + generated clients regenerated and the protocol CI job green, loopback no longer locks out a correct token, keepalive socket option set (assert via getsockopt). Every existing suite must pass; update an existing test only where this stage deliberately changes behaviour and say which and why. Docs: docs/editor.html + docs/logging-and-editor.html + protocol docs (find where the error codes and protocol version are documented: docs/protocol or editor docs) + docs/testing.html; the frontend repo is NOT touched here (a separate frontend PR maps `busy` later). Concurrency risk again: reason about races between preempt/takeover and the session thread's cleanup, the autosave flush, the main thread's command in flight, and a second candidate arriving during a takeover. Unverified items: Windows keepalive options, thread timing on slow runners, anything the frontend does with `busy`. Nothing builds locally; CI (10 checks incl. the `protocol (generated clients, golden vectors)` job) is the test.
acceptance: Preemption by strictly higher role, same-user takeover and no-token newest-takes-over work with clean cleanup of the old session; candidate gets Busy if the old session does not end within 3 s
Protocol 1.13.0 adds the `busy` error code additively; generated clients and golden vectors regenerated; old clients unaffected (plain Error when errorCodes not requested)
Loopback global backoff is replaced by a pre-auth concurrency/rate cap; a correct token is never locked out by loopback failures
TCP keepalive set on session sockets; all existing suites pass unchanged except deliberately changed behaviour (each justified); all 10 checks green; docs updated
notes: Reviewer: races between Preempt/Takeover and the session thread's cleanup/autosave/main-thread command; second candidate during a takeover; the 3 s wait and Busy fallback; protocol change is strictly additive and generated files match the generator output (golden vectors), version asserted everywhere, old-client behaviour unchanged; role comparison correct (strictly higher only); the no-token newest-takes-over cannot be abused beyond the loopback-only default; loopback cap cannot be bypassed to flood nor lock out a correct token; keepalive per OS; docs true. Unverified: Windows keepalive, frontend handling.
